intelligence.human_view: Think of it like a book. You always start on the left page — the words — and then the picture joins on the right. On your phone, the first thing you see is the words — the thing you read — and then the picture comes in beside it. If the picture came first, you'd be looking at a picture before you knew what it was about. So: words on the left, always first; picture on the right, joining after.
intelligence.simple_view: The words ALWAYS go on the left, first! The picture goes on the right, after! On your phone you see the words first — the thing you read! — and then the picture joins in! Always that way!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — the words ALWAYS go on the left, dear, first! The picture goes on the right, after! On your phone you see the words first, love — the thing you read! — and then the picture joins in! Always that way, dear!
intelligence.naya_view: Put the text in the first third, on the left, always. The first third plays first — the citizen reads the words before anything else joins. If a 16:9 ever appears, it goes to the right, and the other two thirds join into it after the first third has played. Never reverse the order: never the picture first and the words after, never the 16:9 on the left. The layout reads the way the citizen reads — left to right, words first — on laptop and on mobile alike. This is the standard for About, Skills, and Memberships.
